maturityDefinitions.educational: Conceptually correct for guided learning, without a claim of independent research-grade validation.
maturityDefinitions.validated: Covered by declared numerical or external oracles inside an explicit parameter and environment scope.
maturityDefinitions.research: Suitable for reproducible investigation when its linked caveats, limitations, and uncertainty are retained.
maturityDefinitions.experimental: Implemented and tested, but not promoted beyond exploratory use or its explicitly measured evidence.

systemCountDefinition.statement: Pendulum Lab publicly documents eight physical-system families under this exact counting rule.
systemCountDefinition.countingRule: Count the eight stable public pendulum-family entry points listed by countedModelIds; do not add SystemSpec variants, Expansion Lab families, stochastic schemes, or analysis-only models to this headline.
exclusions: Point-mass double and compound uniform-rod double are two SystemSpec variants inside the single public double-pendulum family; the variant does not inflate the eight-family headline.
RopePendulum is a dedicated stateful hybrid API rather than a SystemSpec kind, which is why eight public families and eight SystemSpec dispatch kinds are both correct.
Expansion Lab families and independent research modules are intentionally excluded because they use separate maturity and execution contracts.
Aliases, presets, stochastic forcing schemes, and integrator variants never create an additional physical-system family.

models.label: Compound double pendulum with uniform rods

limitations.statement: Physical GPU evidence currently covers Intel only; NVIDIA or AMD behavior and complete vendor certification must not be inferred.
The N-chain GPU path is planar N at most eight and hybrid; nonlinear trajectories and Jacobian tapes remain CPU f64, so it is not a full-GPU trajectory implementation.
The AssemblyScript f64 SIMD N-chain path remains an unpromoted candidate until parity and speedup evidence satisfy its promotion gate.
SharedArrayBuffer side-plot claims require Cloudflare mirror COOP and COEP headers plus a positive crossOriginIsolated deployment probe.
Double-double arithmetic is a short-horizon validation reference and is not presented as a real-time interactive arithmetic path.
Kuramoto and Huygens use phase reduction rather than a full escapement, contact, and clock model; finite-size chimera results remain candidates.
Coulomb and Stribeck regularization does not solve the exact static-friction complementarity cone.
Pyragas delay dynamics use fixed-step RK4 with linear history interpolation and delay at least one step; stability boundaries require step refinement.
Non-commutative matrix noise has no Levy-area construction here, so a strong-order-one claim is prohibited.
Spherical polar coordinates are singular at the poles; near-pole fidelity requires an embedded chart and an explicit caveat.
Neimark-Sacker collocation assumes smooth conjugacy inside its supported regime; Arnold-tongue fallbacks must state their source.
Arclength continuation does not automatically choose the intended branch after a bifurcation.
The video-tracker core is headless and tested, while live camera permission, calibration, occlusion recovery, and webcam UX remain incomplete.
Cycle expansion is truncated; without coefficient-tail and maximum-period refinement it cannot support a definitive claim.
The flagship study centers one frequency, uses a restricted scan and warm-started attractor branch, may miss coexisting basins, and uses first-order Melnikov theory.
The independent Python check uses coarser steps and finite-difference monodromy, supporting tolerance-level reproduction rather than bitwise equality.
MATLAB validation is optional and unpinned; any release claim using it must pin release, toolbox, script, and checksum manifests.
Windows headless WebKit audio instability is environment evidence; user-facing audio needs a fallback and an explicit browser matrix.

process: Triage the numerical discrepancy and assign a severity without changing public artifacts.
Embargo exploitable or misleading details while preserving an immutable incident identifier.
Correct code and regenerate evidence from the exact reviewed source commit.
Revoke every affected artifact digest and force its visible claim to withheld.
Notify affected users and publication channels with impact, correction, and reproduction details.
Close only after the corrected artifact and notification record are independently verified.

severityDefinitions.sev-1: A result-changing physics error that can invalidate published conclusions or safety-relevant interpretation.
severityDefinitions.sev-2: A material numerical error affecting a supported model, evidence status, or a substantial set of exported results.
severityDefinitions.sev-3: A bounded correctness defect with a documented workaround and no known published-conclusion impact.
severityDefinitions.sev-4: A presentation or provenance defect that does not change computed numerical values but still needs correction.

scope.statement: Vitest pass totals recorded for the exact source commit and dependency lock named by the evidence summary.

invalidatedBy: Any failed or incomplete Vitest result invalidates the pass total.
A different source commit or dependency lock requires a newly generated evidence summary.

downgradeRules.reason: Expired or undated test evidence cannot retain a validated public level.
Failed, missing, or indeterminate test results cannot support a public pass-total claim.
A revoked test artifact cannot support a public pass-total claim.
An open investigation or pending correction prevents validated display until resolution.
An embargoed or revoked numerical incident withholds the affected claim.

scope.statement: Maximum trajectory divergence observed only across the regular SciPy reference cases in the cross-validation report.

claims.caveat: Chaotic trajectories use time-amplified tolerances and are not claimed bitwise-identical.
invalidatedBy: A regular reference case exceeding its configured tolerance invalidates passed status.
Changes to the model equations, solver policy, or reference environment require reproduction.

downgradeRules.reason: Expired or undated external-reference evidence cannot retain validated status.
Failed, missing, or indeterminate SciPy comparison results cannot support a public agreement claim.
A revoked cross-validation artifact cannot support a public divergence claim.
An open investigation or pending correction prevents validated display until resolution.
An embargoed or revoked numerical incident withholds the affected claim.

scope.statement: Aggregate mutation score for the committed mutation shards under the repository's 65 percent regression floor.

claims.caveat: Below the 70% quality target; the 65% regression floor is enforced.
invalidatedBy: A score below the configured 65 percent floor invalidates the regression gate.
Missing, stale, or differently configured mutation shards require a new aggregate.

downgradeRules.reason: Expired or undated mutation evidence cannot retain a validated public level.
A mutation score below the quality target remains a measurement, not a validated quality claim.
Failed or unavailable mutation evidence cannot support a visible quality claim.
A revoked mutation artifact cannot support a public score claim.
An open investigation or pending correction prevents validated display until resolution.
An embargoed or revoked numerical incident withholds the affected claim.

scope.statement: Count of integrator methods profiled by the committed energy benchmark at its recorded horizon and step policy.

claims.caveat: Compare each method against its documented order and structure-preservation behavior.
invalidatedBy: Changing the benchmark horizon, initial state, method registry, or step policy requires reproduction.
The lowest drift in one profile does not establish universal accuracy or stability.

downgradeRules.reason: Expired or undated benchmark evidence is retained only as historical information.
Failed, missing, or indeterminate energy benchmark results cannot support a public method-count claim.
A revoked benchmark artifact cannot support a public method-count claim.
An open investigation or pending correction prevents measured display until resolution.
An embargoed or revoked numerical incident withholds the affected claim.

scope.statement: Physical GPU vendors with accepted evidence rows under the committed adapter-matrix promotion contract.

claims.caveat: The matrix is intentionally incomplete until missing physical vendor runners upload evidence. Software adapters do not satisfy this contract.
invalidatedBy: Software adapters, missing provenance, or failed promotion thresholds cannot count as physical vendor evidence.
Kernel, driver, adapter, or promotion-contract changes require new hardware evidence.

downgradeRules.reason: Expired or undated driver evidence cannot retain a validated hardware level.
Partial vendor coverage is a measured subset and cannot imply complete GPU certification.
Failed or unavailable hardware evidence cannot support a vendor-coverage claim.
A revoked GPU artifact cannot support a public vendor-matrix claim.
An open investigation or pending correction prevents validated hardware display until resolution.
An embargoed or revoked numerical incident withholds the affected claim.

scope.statement: Public availability status of the exact package version, GitHub release, reviewer Pages site, and Zenodo record.

claims.caveat: npm registry does not resolve this exact package version. No matching public Zenodo DOI record resolves for Pendulum Lab.
invalidatedBy: A failed public endpoint probe invalidates availability for that publication channel.
A package-version or release-tag change requires a newly generated publication status report.

downgradeRules.reason: Expired or undated endpoint evidence cannot retain a publication-ready level.
Missing npm or DOI publication channels must remain visibly partial.
Failed or unavailable endpoint evidence cannot support a publication claim.
A revoked publication artifact cannot support public availability.
An open investigation or pending correction prevents publication-ready display until resolution.
An embargoed or revoked numerical incident withholds the affected claim.
